# OpenMotion OpenMotion is **the first full-stack agentic video generator**. Upload a reference video or paste a social video link to **recreate it with your own brand kit (logo, colors and fonts) and copy**. - 🎬 **Full-stack video recreation.** Code video with HTML. Your agent breaks down the reference, rebuilds its shots and transitions, and generates missing assets. Edit the timing in Studio and render an MP4 from the same project. - 🔑 **BYOA — Bring Your Own Agent. BYOK — Bring Your Own Keys.** OpenMotion is free and open source. Recreate videos in [your local agent](#agent-wall) and use your own API keys at every layer. - 🧩 OpenMotion introduces **Motion.md**, a Markdown format for shot order, timing and transitions. Use it to share how a brand film works, shot by shot. - 🎛️ **Images, video, music and voice.** Generate artwork with Nano Banana 2, add a shot with Seedance 2.0, score it with Suno v4 and narrate it with Kokoro. [Explore all seven built-in models](#model-wall). **22 local agents** · [Choose your agent](#choose-agent)

[Get agent prompts for all seven use cases](docs/examples.md) ## ✨ Why OpenMotion ### 1. The first full-stack agentic video generator **Code video with HTML.** OpenMotion uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript to describe scenes, typography, layout, transitions and timing. Recorded footage, generated clips, images, music and voice-over become media inside the composition. The same project opens in Studio and renders to MP4. ![Your local agent, optional media-model accounts and creative resources feed a workflow of understanding the reference, coding scenes, generating missing media, editing and rendering MP4 with reusable source.](docs/readme/diagrams/creation-stack.svg) **Write it. Watch it. Change it. Render it.** Ask your agent to replace the product, tighten the hook, add a presenter, change the captions or try another ending. It edits the project source; you review the result in the visual editor. Local MCP clients use the project tools, while agents with shell access can follow the Skills and pinned CLI workflow. [Agent setup](#agent-setup) · [Native composition guide](skills/motion-production/references/native.md) · [Example HTML project](template-library/product-promo/index.html) If historical media are unavailable, an Agent restore is refused before changing the project. The editor shows a dismissible error with the affected file paths and confirms that the current project is unchanged. #### What you can change in Studio | In the Studio | What you can do today | | --- | --- | | **Story and timeline** | Import and arrange media; have the agent trim, reorder and revise against a script or confirmed timecodes | | **Motion and captions** | Author animated type, transitions, callouts, charts and captions around your content | | **Media and sound** | Import your material and generate images, video, music and TTS voice-over through the built-in model integrations | | **Image revision** | Generate candidates with a reference-capable image model and adopt a replacement while preserving timing and animation | | **Preview and versions** | Review in Studio, edit by hand or with your agent, and return to the project for the next revision | | **Export and source** | Render a fixed version to MP4 and retain the HTML, CSS, JavaScript and media | > “Keep the reveal we approved. Replace the middle scene with this screen recording, tighten the opening using these timecodes, and hold our final CTA for two more seconds.” [Projects and versions](docs/project-workspace.md) #### From a reference clip to an editable remake 1. **Break down the reference.** Pick a sequence. Record its shot order, transitions and sound cues in Motion.md, and mark what you want to replace. 2. **Rebuild the shots.** Your agent rebuilds the HTML scenes using your brand kit, copy and visuals, then arranges them on an editable timeline in Studio. 3. **Compare the cuts.** Watch the same moment in the original and the remake. Adjust the timing, movement and sound, then play the sequence through. 4. **Export and share.** Render the MP4 and keep the HTML source and media. To share a project others can adapt, include its Motion.md, a preview and assets you can redistribute. [Project contribution checklist](library/ENTRY_TEMPLATE.md) ### 2. Free and open source. Use your local agent and bring your own keys. **Choose your agent.** WorkBuddy, Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness have installation instructions. Other buttons open the shared MCP and CLI setup.

| Bring your own… | Make it work for your video | | --- | --- | | **🤖 Agent — BYOA** | Connect your existing local agent through Skills and MCP, with CLI access where supported. Keep your preferred client, account and working context. | | **🔑 Keys — BYOK** | Connect supported media-provider API keys in Model Settings. Choose models for images, video, music and TTS; supported local media integrations can use your existing agent login. | | **🎨 Brand and material** | Add your logo, fonts, screenshots, camera footage, script and music. Keep identity and approved assets in the Brand Kit section of Motion.md. | | **🧩 Starting resources** | Browse references, motion components, templates and community Skills. Pick a direction, give the source or reference to your agent, and make it yours. | **The OpenMotion creation pipeline is open source: Skills, project tools, model integrations, Studio and rendering.** Run it locally, inspect the implementation and extend the parts you need. OpenMotion charges no software subscription or per-render fee for this local workflow. You can also work with your own footage, images and audio without invoking media-generation APIs. Provider credentials stay in your workspace, separate from the video project. Your agent and media providers bill any subscriptions or usage to your own accounts. Add the selected results to the recreated project, align the sound and visuals, then show me the full cut.” [Model catalog](gateway/catalog.ts) · [Provider setup and endpoints](docs/model-gateway.md) ## 🛠️ Setup and technical documentation ### Quick start For any successful Agent-led installation, follow the [installation reply rules and examples](docs/install.md#installation-success-reply) in the current conversation; setup provides real template summaries. Invite before creation and preserve the accepted template. For a packaged install, give your agent the [test installation guide](https://releases.open-design.ai/open-motion/dev/install.md). It pins the package version and walks through isolated setup. To run from source, follow the steps below. If MCP tools are missing or fail to connect, use the installed [connection diagnosis and recovery guide](docs/npm-installation.md#missing-mcp-tools-or-a-failed-connection) to inspect the actual host configuration and verify the original workspace before continuing. Use Git, npm and **Node.js 26.11.1**. Source-based preview and export also need Chrome/Chromium and FFmpeg/FFprobe. [Runtime setup](docs/usage.md) ```sh git clone --branch feature/motion https://github.com/nexu-io/html-anything.git openmotion cd openmotion npm ci npm run build:studio npm start ``` Open **http://localhost:4173**. Choose **Templates → Ready to edit**, open **Product Promo**, and use **Connect Agent** for your preferred client. Keep projects and credentials outside the checkout; `MOTION_DATA_DIR` selects the workspace. #### Bring it into your agent For Codex with plugin support, run from the checkout: ```sh bash scripts/install-motion.command ``` **WorkBuddy** · Import the OpenMotion connector in WorkBuddy or add its `mcp.json` as a custom MCP server. Ask WorkBuddy to list the available video templates. [WorkBuddy setup](docs/agent-adapters.md#workbuddy) **Claude Code** · Select `--host claude` in the local installer, then run `/mcp` in Claude Code to check the connection. [Local installation guide](docs/npm-installation.md) **DeepSeek** · Work with the editable HTML project from the terminal in DeepSeek TUI. For DeepSeek Harness, connect the OpenMotion MCP tools with the Cordis configuration. [DeepSeek Harness setup](docs/agent-adapters.md#deepseek-harness) The installer uses locally built packages. [Windows test packages](docs/test-packages.md) Try the included template first: > Use OpenMotion to open a fresh copy of the 20-second Product Promo in Studio and export an MP4. Keep the editable project. Then make it yours: > Keep the structure and animation. Replace the logo, screenshots, headline and end card with my supplied brand materials. Show the new cut, then hold the final title two seconds longer. To start from a video instead, supply your reference and use the [recreation brief](#reverse-engineer-a-video). If your host cannot open Studio beside the conversation, use the returned local project link. New test npm builds embed **DEV** template defaults; stable packages embed **prod**. Existing published versions keep their original defaults. The environment is stored in the package, so Studio and MCP agree without setup-only environment variables. Use isolated test host, application and data directories. See [test installation and template configuration](docs/npm-installation.md#test-template-data-dev) and the [test publication manual](docs/release-workflows.md). ##### Skills, MCP and CLI From the checkout, discover and install the five core workflows with the [Skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): ```sh npx skills add ./skills --list npx skills add ./skills --skill motion-director motion-production motion-template-to-video motion-recreate motion-video-to-template ``` This copies instructions; it does not install the runtime or register MCP. In a shell-based agent, open the project directory and use the [local engine CLI](skills/motion-production/references/native.md) to preview and render the HTML scenes. ```json { "mcpServers": { "openmotion": { "command": "/absolute/path/to/node", "args": ["--experimental-strip-types", "/absolute/openmotion/mcp.ts"], "env": { "MOTION_DATA_DIR": "/absolute/openmotion-data" } } } } ``` The **eleven public MCP tools** cover template discovery and details, project creation and reading, editing, preview, media import, export, version restoration and cancellation. Start from the reference with the [recreation workflow](skills/motion-recreate/SKILL.md), or use the [template workflow](skills/motion-template-to-video/SKILL.md) when you already have editable source. ```text Use OpenMotion to reverse-engineer the attached reference for our brand. Study: the opening hook, shot order, typography, transitions and sound cues. Keep: the product reveal and camera rhythm in the selected segment. Replace: the logo, UI, claims, copy and end card with our supplied materials. Generate: missing images, video, background music and TTS narration using our configured models, following our brand and approved script. Build an editable project. Open it in Studio and compare matching moments with the reference. Explain any remaining differences. After review, export an MP4 and retain the source for the next edit. ``` #### Start in your agent ![OpenMotion embedded viewer for Codex, showing the editable Product Promo project, preview, layers and timeline.](docs/readme/product-tour/codex-embedded.png) #### Start in Studio Browse references, open a template or bring in your recordings. Choose **Connect Agent**, follow the workspace-specific instructions and give the agent your brief. Review its edits on the same timeline and make hands-on adjustments whenever you want. ![Standalone OpenMotion Studio with sessions, the saved request and an editable video project.](docs/readme/product-tour/standalone-studio.png) #### Connect your agent to a template ![Connect Agent dialog with workspace-specific connection instructions and a choice of local clients.](docs/readme/product-tour/connect-agent.png) ![Product Promo template preview with an expanded, template-specific instruction to copy into the agent.](docs/readme/product-tour/template-to-agent.png) **Preview → copy the instruction → paste into your agent with your brand assets.** A bundled template opens as an editable copy; an external reference starts a reconstruction task. [Full product tour](docs/product-tour.md) Both entry paths use the same local application and project. The agent runs in its own client; Studio stores the brief and editable work. [How the connection works](docs/session-architecture.md) ### System architecture Editing the timeline in Studio and asking your agent to change a shot both update the same HTML project. The local TypeScript service manages media and revisions. A browser-based rendering engine exports the selected version to MP4. #### How the modules work together ![The local agent connects through nine MCP project tools and Studio through local HTTP. The application manages revisions, assets and export jobs; the Model Gateway supplies media to the editable project, and the renderer exports and checks the selected project version.](docs/readme/diagrams/runtime-architecture-painterly.png) Edits made through the project tools include a revision check so an outdated request cannot overwrite newer work. Generated media enters the project when you select it. Each export uses the version saved when the job starts. The exporter checks the file specifications, and you can play the cut to review the picture, sound and timing.
